subject.title: feat(cron): shell precheck gate to skip LLM when no work

question: Should cron expose `precheck` as a second persisted host-shell gate, or should the existing condition-trigger contract be extended to cover the intended no-work decision before a payload starts?
rationale: Both paths affect the durable cron-job API, operator documentation, execution ordering, and security expectations; source review cannot determine which long-term user contract maintainers want.

options.title: Extend the existing trigger contract
options.body: Keep one canonical cron gate and add a governed host-command mode only if its distinct no-model behavior is required.

options.title: Approve a separate precheck contract
options.body: Retain `precheck` as an intentionally distinct host-shell probe and document its ordering, ownership, and semantic differences from condition triggers.

options.title: Narrow and defer the feature
options.body: Pause this branch until a maintainer-sponsored design specifies the public cron gate contract.

recommendation.title: Extend the existing trigger contract
recommendation.body: Keep one canonical cron gate and add a governed host-command mode only if its distinct no-model behavior is required.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership could not be established reliably from the supplied review context; the decision should route to the cron/Gateway feature owner identified by maintainer history.
